query: I'm new to investing and have student loans. What should I prioritize first with my savings?

recommendations.title: Complete Emergency Fund Before Increasing Investments
recommendations.summary: Prioritize building your 6-month emergency fund ($22,000) in high-yield savings before allocating more to investments given your lack of emergency reserves, moderate debt, and conservative risk tolerance.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With no emergency fund, $38,000 in debt (likely student loans), and only $15,000 in cash against $25,000 total assets, you're financially vulnerable. Your conservative risk tolerance (loss comfort 3/10) and beginner experience mean market volatility could cause significant stress. At 28 with stable income ($72,000) and monthly expenses of $3,800, you need $22,800 in liquid reserves. Current investment allocation (40% in VTTSX/BND) is appropriate for your profile, but adding more now increases risk exposure before securing your financial foundation. High-yield savings accounts currently offer 4-5% APY with zero risk, which aligns perfectly with your emergency fund goal timeline and risk tolerance.
recommendations.suggested_action: Maintain current investment positions while directing all additional savings ($1,200-$1,500/month after expenses) to a high-yield savings account until emergency fund reaches $22,000

recommendations.title: Optimize Debt Paydown Strategy Alongside Savings
recommendations.summary: Evaluate interest rates on your $38,000 debt and aggressively pay down any loans above 6% interest while building emergency savings, as debt reduction provides guaranteed returns.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your $38,000 debt load against $25,000 assets creates negative net worth of -$13,000, which is a significant financial burden. As a junior data analyst earning $72,000, student loans are likely your primary debt. If any carry interest rates above 6%, paying these down provides guaranteed returns exceeding most conservative investments. With $1,200-$1,500 monthly surplus after $3,800 expenses, consider a split strategy: 60% to emergency fund, 40% to high-interest debt (above 6%). For loans below 5%, minimum payments are acceptable while you build reserves. This balanced approach addresses both liquidity needs and guaranteed 'return' through debt reduction, particularly important given your medium liquidity needs and moderate debt classification.
recommendations.suggested_action: Analyze debt interest rates; allocate 40% of monthly savings ($480-$600) toward loans above 6% APR while maintaining 60% to emergency fund

recommendations.title: Maintain Conservative Portfolio Mix for Beginner Profile
recommendations.summary: Your current 30% target-date fund (VTTSX) and 10% bond (BND) allocation is appropriate for your beginner experience and conservative risk tolerance; avoid adding equity exposure until emergency fund is complete.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: VTTSX (Vanguard Target Retirement 2060) provides age-appropriate diversification with approximately 90% stocks/10% bonds internally, automatically rebalancing over time. Combined with BND (Vanguard Total Bond Market), your invested $10,000 (40% of assets) has reasonable diversification. For a 28-year-old beginner with conservative risk tolerance and loss comfort of only 3/10, this is actually slightly aggressive but acceptable given your medium investment horizon. The 60% cash position reflects your emergency fund needs appropriately. Do NOT increase equity exposure or chase higher returns until you have 3-6 months expenses saved. Your house down payment goal ($60,000 in 5-7 years) can be addressed after emergency fund completion through increased conservative investments.
recommendations.suggested_action: Hold existing positions without additional contributions; review and rebalance only after emergency fund reaches $15,000+ milestone

recommendations.title: Open High-Yield Savings Account for Emergency Fund
recommendations.summary: Immediately move your $15,000 cash into a high-yield savings account earning 4-5% APY to maximize returns while maintaining full liquidity for emergency needs.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your 60% cash allocation ($15,000) is likely sitting in a traditional checking or low-yield savings account earning under 0.5% APY. High-yield savings accounts from institutions like Marcus, Ally, Capital One 360, or American Express currently offer 4.0-5.0% APY with FDIC insurance, no fees, and full liquidity. This represents $600-$750 in annual interest versus $75 in traditional savings—a meaningful difference when building toward $22,000 emergency fund. Given your conservative risk tolerance, medium liquidity needs, and stable income, HYSA provides optimal balance: zero market risk, immediate access, and competitive returns. As a beginner, this is an actionable first step that builds good financial habits. Takes 10-15 minutes to open online with no minimum balance requirements.
recommendations.suggested_action: Transfer entire $15,000 cash position to high-yield savings account within 1 week; set up automatic monthly deposits of $1,200-$1,500
